title: Perplexity SEO: what transfers from Google, with 2026 data
meta_description: Perplexity SEO with 2026 data: how often its citations overlap Google's top 10, which sources it prefers, and the practical steps that get you cited.
og_title: Perplexity is the AI engine where SEO transfers best. Partly.
og_description: Between 13% and 39% of the URLs Perplexity cites rank in Google's top 10, depending on the study. Here is what carries over from SEO, what does not, and what to do.
h1: Perplexity SEO: what transfers from Google, what does not, and how to get cited
card_title: Perplexity SEO: what actually transfers from Google
card_summary: Perplexity's citations overlap with Google's top 10 more than ChatGPT's do, but most of what it cites still sits outside it. This guide compares three overlap studies, shows Perplexity's source mix for November 2026 and lists the steps that matter.
extract_html: Perplexity is the AI engine where classic SEO transfers best: depending on the study, between about 13% and 39% of the URLs it cites also rank in Google's top 10 for the same query, well above ChatGPT in the two studies that report both. The best 2026 figure is 39.4%, from 8,562 Perplexity citations collected in May 2026[2]. So Google rankings help, but most Perplexity citations still go to pages outside the top 10, and Reddit, YouTube and Wikipedia take a large share[4].
body_html:
Does SEO work for Perplexity?

Yes, more than for any other major AI assistant, but only partly. Perplexity runs its own crawler, PerplexityBot, and does not simply borrow Google's or Bing's index[1]. Even so, the pages it cites overlap with Google's top 10 far more than ChatGPT's do, in both studies we checked that report figures for each.

Why that happens is inferred, not proven. Perplexity was designed as an answer engine with sources shown up front, and the things that make a page rank in Google (it is crawlable, it matches the query, other sites link to it, it answers clearly) are also what a retrieval system looks for. So the useful question is not whether SEO helps. It is which parts transfer, which do not, and what Perplexity adds on top. If you want the wider comparison first, our piece on how GEO differs from SEO covers it.

How much do Perplexity's citations overlap with Google's top 10?

Between about 13% and 39% of cited URLs, depending on how you measure, which means most Perplexity citations do not rank in Google's top 10 for the same query. Three studies have looked at it directly.

Share of Perplexity-cited URLs that also rank in Google's top 10 for the same query, by study (sources checked November 2026).
StudyData collectedSamplePerplexity URLs in Google top 10Comparison
Ahrefs[1]Early July 202515,000 long-tail queries, Brand Radar28.6%ChatGPT in-text citations: 8.0%
OrganiKPI[2]May 20265,000 queries, 6 platforms, 8,562 Perplexity citations39.4% (50.25% at domain level)Gemini: 41.1%. All platforms: 23.05%
Orbit Media[3]To 23 August 202672 prompts, 3 B2B brands, 13,184 citations across 4 tools13% to 23%Gemini and ChatGPT: roughly 1% to 5%

The spread is a method problem more than a contradiction. Ahrefs used long-tail queries, where the top 10 is a thin slice of what could answer the question. OrganiKPI matched cited URLs against the organic top 10 for the same query across 25 categories[2]. Orbit Media's author describes his 72-prompt tracker as a directional sample, not statistical proof, and only compared prompts he could map to a keyword[3].

The direction is consistent, though. Ranking well in Google is a real advantage in Perplexity, and a bigger one than in ChatGPT. It is not a guarantee and it is not a requirement: even in the highest estimate, 60.6% of Perplexity's citations went to pages outside the top 10.

Read more: why a separate index can still look like Google

Ahrefs notes that Perplexity does not draw on Google's or Bing's index and uses PerplexityBot instead[1]. Two independent systems can still agree a lot if they reward similar things. Our working theory is that Perplexity searches with phrasing closer to the user's question than ChatGPT does, so its results resemble a normal search more. That is a hypothesis. Perplexity has not published how it ranks sources, and we have not seen a study that tests it.

What sources does Perplexity prefer?

Community and video platforms, followed by reference and retail sites. In Ahrefs' Brand Radar data for November 2026, covering more than 3.1 million US queries, Reddit took 24.6% of citations among Perplexity's top 50 sources, YouTube 14.2% and Wikipedia 7.2%, followed by Amazon at 4.3% and Facebook at 3.1%[4]. Healthline (2.9%) and the New York Times (2.0%) also make the top 10.

Two cautions before you act on that. First, Ahrefs calculates mention share against the summed citations of the top sources, not against every citation, so it overstates any one domain's share of the whole. Second, the mix depends heavily on the questions. Orbit Media's B2B tracker found Perplexity's favourite sources were LinkedIn (374 citations), YouTube (248) and Reddit (232), and in its most recent weekly run Reddit was just 3% of Perplexity's citations[3]. Consumer questions pull in Reddit and Amazon. B2B questions pull in LinkedIn. The source mix that matters is the one for your prompts.

Perplexity also cites a lot of sources per answer: 19.2 on average in Orbit Media's data[3]. That leaves room in an answer for more than the obvious category leader, which is good news for smaller sites. We cover the Reddit side in detail in how Reddit feeds AI search.

Does Perplexity favour fresh content?

Less than the folklore claims. In Ahrefs' analysis of about 17 million citations, published in July 2025, Perplexity's in-text citations averaged 1,166 days since publication, against 1,416 days for organic Google results in the same table[5]. That is fresher than Google, but it was the oldest of the four assistants measured: Gemini averaged 1,118 days, Copilot 1,056 and ChatGPT 958 to 1,023, depending on citation type.

Ahrefs also found that Perplexity seems to order its in-text references from newest to oldest[5]. Confidence label: evidenced but dated. The data predates 2026, and Ahrefs does not state the collection window. Updating a page with genuinely new information is sensible. Changing the date without changing the content is folklore, and we would not spend time on it.

How do you get cited by Perplexity?

Make sure PerplexityBot can reach you, keep the Google work that already earns rankings, and then add the parts Perplexity weighs that Google does not. In order of how sure we are:

  1. Let PerplexityBot in (evidenced). Perplexity's crawler documentation recommends allowing PerplexityBot in robots.txt and permitting requests from its published IP ranges. It says PerplexityBot exists to surface and link websites in Perplexity's search results, not to crawl content for foundation models[6]. Check your firewall and CDN bot rules as well as robots.txt, because either can block it. Perplexity says changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
  2. Protect the rankings you already have (evidenced). In two of the three studies above, roughly 3 in 10 or more of Perplexity's citations ranked in Google's top 10. Existing top-10 pages are your cheapest Perplexity asset. Do not rewrite them into something thinner for AI.
  3. Answer first, in a passage that stands alone (inferred). An answer engine quotes passages, not pages. Put the direct answer in the first sentence under each heading, with the number and its date, so the passage still makes sense when lifted out.
  4. Be present on the platforms it cites for your category (evidenced for the mix, inferred for the effect). For consumer topics that means Reddit, YouTube and Wikipedia-style reference pages[4]. For B2B, LinkedIn showed up first in one tracker[3]. Earn mentions there honestly; astroturfing gets removed and damages trust.
  5. Cover the long tail Google ignores (inferred). Most Perplexity citations sit outside Google's top 10, so specific pages for specific questions (comparisons, pricing, edge cases) give Perplexity something to cite where your Google rankings are thin.
  6. Update with substance (evidenced but dated). Fresher pages appear to be listed earlier in Perplexity's references[5]. Add new data, not a new date.

What does not transfer from Google SEO?

Position, measurement and traffic assumptions. There is no stable rank in Perplexity. Orbit Media found it was the most stable of the four engines it tracked, yet only 65% of cited URLs survived between runs two days apart[3]. A single check tells you very little.

Your Google tools do not see Perplexity either. Search Console reports Google impressions, not Perplexity citations. And nobody has published a click-through rate for Perplexity citations that we would trust, so do not model Perplexity traffic with Google CTR curves. Treat citations as visibility first and measure referral visits separately.

How should you measure Perplexity visibility?

Run a fixed set of real customer questions repeatedly and record who gets mentioned and which URLs get cited. That is the method we use: a prompt set built from sales calls and search data, run on a schedule in tracking tools such as Peec, with Perplexity reported separately from ChatGPT and Google's AI answers, because their source habits differ. Pair it with referral sessions from perplexity.ai in your analytics, which show whether citations turn into visits.

The same logic applies to every engine, but the levers differ. Our guide to how ChatGPT retrieves and selects sources covers the engine where Google rankings help least. If you want to know where you stand in Perplexity today, the free AI visibility audit runs your category's questions and shows who gets cited instead of you.

faq.a: Perplexity SEO is the work of getting your pages cited and your brand mentioned in Perplexity's answers. It overlaps with Google SEO more than optimisation for any other AI engine, because studies find 13% to 39% of Perplexity's cited URLs also rank in Google's top 10. It adds crawler access for PerplexityBot, answer-first passages and presence on the platforms Perplexity cites, such as Reddit and YouTube.

faq.q: How do I get cited by Perplexity?
faq.a: Allow PerplexityBot in robots.txt and in your firewall, keep the pages that already rank in Google's top 10 strong, and put a direct, dated answer at the top of each section. Build presence on the sites Perplexity cites for your category, such as Reddit, YouTube or LinkedIn, and publish specific pages for long-tail questions. Then sample real prompts repeatedly to see whether citations move.

faq.q: Does ranking in Google help you rank in Perplexity?
faq.a: Yes, more than it helps in ChatGPT. Ahrefs found 28.6% of Perplexity's cited URLs ranked in Google's top 10 in July 2025, against 8.0% for ChatGPT's in-text citations, and a May 2026 study put Perplexity at 39.4%. But the majority of Perplexity citations still come from pages outside the top 10, so Google rankings help without being required.

Only if you do not want to appear in Perplexity's answers. Perplexity says PerplexityBot is used to surface and link websites in its search results, not to train foundation models, and recommends allowing it. Blocking it removes your pages from its index. Note that Perplexity-User, which fetches a page when a user asks, generally ignores robots.txt according to Perplexity's own documentation.

sources: Ahrefs, "Only 12% of AI Cited URLs Rank in Google's Top 10 for the Original Prompt", Louise Linehan with Xibeijia Guan, 11 August 2025. 15,000 long-tail queries via Brand Radar, data collected early July 2025.

OrganiKPI, "Google Killed Text Fragments in AI Mode. Here Is What 153,425 Citations Say to Do About It", Daniel Shashko, May 2026 (updated August 2026). 5,000 queries across 25 categories and 6 platforms, 8,562 Perplexity citations, collected May 2026. Self-published study.

Orbit Media, "I Tracked 13,184 AI Citations Across 4 LLMs: Here's What I Learned", Bill Widmer, 2 September 2026. 72 prompts across 3 B2B brands, weekly runs, data through 23 August 2026. Directional sample.

Ahrefs, "The 50 Most-Cited Websites in Perplexity (November 2026)", Si Quan Ong, updated 3 November 2026. Brand Radar, more than 3.1 million US queries, all topics; share calculated against the top 50 sources.
Ahrefs, "New Study: AI Assistants Prefer to Cite 'Fresher' Content (17 Million Citations Analyzed)", Ryan Law with Xibeijia Guan, 28 July 2025. Brand Radar; collection period not stated.
Perplexity, "Perplexity Crawlers", developer documentation, undated, accessed November 2026.
